canonical_name: backoff 2.2.1 -- exponential backoff with jitter as Python decorators (litl)
lineage: The retry rule of Ethernet (binary exponential backoff, 1973-76) and of TCP RTO, packaged for application code; jitter follows the 'full jitter' analysis (Brooker, AWS Architecture Blog 2015). A small mechanism: wait = min(cap, base * 2^n) * random.

example.command: python harness: generate the wait sequence of expo with and without full_jitter
example.output: the wait schedule and its spread

upstream_docs: Brooker, Exponential Backoff And Jitter, AWS Architecture Blog, 2015
Metcalfe & Boggs, Ethernet, CACM 1976 (binary exponential backoff)

human_capability_summary.built_to: spread retries out in time, and de-synchronise many retriers so they do not collide again
human_capability_summary.pressure: a shared resource that fails under simultaneous demand; retries that re-collide if scheduled identically
human_capability_summary.success_means: the retrying population thins out geometrically and desynchronises; the resource recovers

human_environmental_pressure: contention on a shared resource, transient failure
human_failure_condition: synchronised retry storm: every client retries at the same instant and the resource never recovers
behavioral_entry_point: compare the wait schedules of expo vs full_jitter over many clients: identical versus spread

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run backoff-2.2.1
